newsitem.title: USA: Tyco to acquire ADT Ltd for $5.6 billion.
newsitem.headline: Tyco to acquire ADT Ltd for $5.6 billion.

text.p: Tyco International Ltd, solidifying its position as the world's largest provider of fire and safety systems, said Monday it entered a definitive agreement to acquire ADT Ltd for $5.6 billion in stock, topping a hostile takeover bid by Western Resources Inc.

Tyco, a diversified maker of industrial and commercial products, said that under terms of the deal ADT stockholders will receive the equivalent of $29 for each share they own, based on Tyco's stock closing price of $60.25 Friday.
The agreed price tops a hostile takeover bid by Western Resources under which ADT stockholders were to receive $22.50 a share, or a total of $3.5 billion.
Shares of ADT, a leading installer and servicer of electronic security systems, closed Friday at $21.75.
Tyco, which is based in Exeter, N.H., said that under the agreement it will merge with a subsidiary of ADT and the ADT parent will be renamed Tyco International Ltd.
Tyco shareholders will receive one share in the combined company for each Tyco share and ADT shareholders will receive 0.48133 shares in the combined company for each ADT share.
After the closing of the deal, Tyco shareholders will own about 64 percent of the outstanding shares of the new company and ADT shareholders will own the remaining 36 percent.
L. Dennis Kozlowski will remain chairman and chief executive of Tyco, which is expected to have annual revenues in excess of $8.5 billion after the merger, the announcement said.
"Tyco's acquisition of ADT is a continuation of our strategy to expand our position in service businesses through internal growth and complementary acquisitions," Kozlowski said in a statement.

ADT, which is based in Boca Raton, Fla., is the largest provider of electronic security services in North America and Britain, with more than 1.8 million industrial, commercial and residential customers. It had revenues of $1.7 billion last year.
The merger will combine ADT's 230 offices in 10 countries with Tyco's Fire and Safety Services group's 300 offices in more than 50 countries.
"ADT's commercial and industrial businesses are an excellent fit with Tyco's Fire and Safety Services group," ADT Chairman and Chief Executive Michael A. Ashcroft said.
"This merger will enhance ADT's ability to continue its growth, not only in North America and the United Kingdom, but in all parts of the world utilizing Tyco's established infrastructure."
In December ADT rejected the unsolicited cash and stock offer from Western Resources, saying the offer was inadequate and would not result in a strong strategic combination.
Officials of Western Resources, an electricity supplier in Topeka, Kan., were not immediately available to comment.
